$comment: Ruvyxa resolves a URL to a route in two languages that cannot share code:
the Rust router in crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/router.rs (dev and `start`),
and the single JavaScript matcher in packages/@ruvyxa/core/src/route-match.ts
(browser router, serverless handler, standalone server). If they disagree, a
soft navigation renders a different page than a reload of the same address —
a defect that only appears after deployment.
Add a case here first when changing matching behaviour; a port that drifts
then fails in the language that drifted, not in review.
$canonicalComment: Raw request path to its canonical segment form, or null when the path must
be refused outright. Refusal is not 'no route': an encoded separator or a
traversal component would let a URL address a route it does not name, so
every host rejects it before matching.
$matchComment: Canonical path to the route pattern that must win and the parameters it
must bind. `route: null` means no route matched — a 404, not a refusal.
An optional catch-all that captured nothing omits its key entirely, so
a page can tell '/shop' apart from '/shop/<segment>'.
Every path here must already be canonical and free of percent-escapes.
The Rust router matches a path that canonical_request_path has already
decoded, while the JavaScript matcher canonicalizes internally — feeding
an escape to both would decode it once on one side and twice on the other
and compare two different requests. Percent-decoding belongs in the
`canonical` table above, which is where it is actually decided.
